name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedRepresentation
title: The selected GNS representation of a pure-state class

content.display_title: The selected GNS representation of a pure-state class
content.one_sentence_role: A choice of representative pure states, fixed literally at a root, gives one concrete GNS representation per equivalence class.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex C*-algebra, with the positive order used for its states, and fix a pure state $\omega$. A pure state is an extreme point of the normalized positive continuous linear functionals. Let $I$ be the set of pure-state GNS representations modulo unitary equivalence. For each $j\in I$, choose a pure state $\varphi_j$ in that class, retaining $\varphi_o=\omega$ literally at $o=[\omega]$. Write $(H_j,\pi_j,\xi_j)$ for its GNS space, representation and canonical cyclic vector. The selected representation is the GNS action $\pi_j:A\to B(H_j)$ associated to this particular $\varphi_j$. The choice concerns the representative state; the construction then uses its actual GNS Hilbert space and action.
content.definition_explanation: Take the chosen state $\varphi_j$, regard it as a positive linear functional, and form its GNS completion $H_j$. Left multiplication induces the bounded action $\pi_j$ on that completion. The selected vector $\xi_j$ is the GNS cyclic vector. Its orbit $\pi_j(A)\xi_j$ is dense. The vector-functional identity and purity of $\varphi_j$, together with this cyclicity and normalization, supply the separate irreducibility theorem.
content.assumptions: The class $j\in I$ and the root pure state $\omega$ are given. GNS representations here are unital complex-linear star homomorphisms on complete complex Hilbert spaces. No separability or faithfulness of $\pi_j$ is assumed.
content.conclusion: The definition specifies $\pi_j$ on $H_j$. The separate selected-vector and pure-GNS results give $\|\xi_j\|=1$, $\varphi_j(a)=\langle\xi_j,\pi_j(a)\xi_j\rangle$, and irreducibility of $\pi_j$. These properties explain why this selected family supplies the summands of the direct-sum representation.
content.lean_realization_notes: The inner product is conjugate linear in its first argument. Irreducibility means that the only closed reducing subspaces are $0$ and $H_j$; this Hilbert space is nonzero because it contains the unit vector $\xi_j$. The definition does not itself prove those properties, and it does not claim that different pure states always have inequivalent GNS representations.
